// Must-NOT-trip fixture: the scan distinguishes the seam from the escape rather
// than banning all file I/O in the scanned packages.
package scanfixture

import (
	"io/fs"

	"github.com/Rivil/dross/internal/pathfence"
)

func readThroughSeam(c pathfence.Contained) ([]byte, error) {
	return pathfence.ReadFile(c)
}

func writeThroughSeam(c pathfence.Contained, body []byte, mode fs.FileMode) error {
	return pathfence.WriteFile(c, body, mode)
}

func statThroughSeam(c pathfence.Contained) (fs.FileInfo, error) {
	return pathfence.Stat(c)
}

// Accessors are fine everywhere EXCEPT inside an os.* argument: this formats
// for a human and opens nothing.
func describe(c pathfence.Contained) string {
	return "doc " + c.Rel() + " (at " + c.String() + ")"
}

// Assigning first is the documented remedy for the type-blind case: the
// accessor call is no longer inside the os.* argument.
func assignFirst(c pathfence.Contained) ([]byte, error) {
	p := c.String()
	return readRaw(p)
}

func readRaw(p string) ([]byte, error) { return nil, nil }
